blocks.note: first meaning: to lock up premises, as a shopkeeper does at night
second meaning: to make someone stop talking

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it look like a single idea of nearly falling silent; it is two separate senses of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to lock premises for the night and to make someone stop talking.

clue.text: Woman's wild boar devours four ungulates, say

definitions.note: ungulates are an example; the answer is the wider group of plant eaters

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the animal run loose into a new order
to devour is to swallow, so one set of letters takes the number inside it

blocks.note: a woman's thing is hers, giving the possessive pronoun
taken as written
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A woman's untamed pig eats four hoofed animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Wild boar reads as the name of one animal, but wild is the signal to rearrange; ungulates are hoofed mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbivora are plant-eating mammals, and hoofed grazers such as cattle, deer and horses are a classic example.

clue.text: UN quits panel sitting in judgment of a group

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so those two letters depart from the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
a tribunal is a body appointed to adjudicate disputes

explanation.surface: The United Nations walks out of a court hearing about a particular group.
explanation.walkthrough: UN looks like the United Nations; it is just the two letters taken out of TRIBUNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal is the adjective for a tribe, a community or group of people bound by kinship.

indicators.note: in a down entry, lying below means coming later in the column

blocks.note: a pole is a post
mica is a flaky silicate mineral
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A disputed rock sample left lying beneath a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing or speech attacks opinions forcefully, so it is contentious and provokes dispute.

blocks.note: first meaning: a tight spot or predicament
second meaning: vegetables kept in vinegar or brine

explanation.walkthrough: Jam and preserve look like the same thing on a breakfast table; here jam means a fix or difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a difficult situation, and also any food kept in vinegar or brine as a relish.

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the initial letter of Police
rang, as in telephoned

explanation.surface: The police are the first ones summoned to a road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is informal British slang for a collision or accident involving a car or aircraft.

blocks.note: to cause is to make something happen
as in make way, meaning make room

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear space so an elevated walkway can go through.
explanation.walkthrough: Make room reads as one phrase meaning make way; split it into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a road or track built up on an embankment across marshy ground or water.

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the phrase before it is used

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Fix a bell up at the top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a heavy bamboo staff, iron-bound, carried by police in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The lathi is a long wooden club or staff used in South Asia, so it is a stick.

clue.text: Drink put down by fantastic bird is rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the joined words are read from the end

blocks.note: put down, as a carpet or an egg
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: Someone's drink has been knocked over by a mythical creature and turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc, a crossword regular, is the enormous bird in the tales of Sinbad.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet fruit concentrate diluted with water, or a liqueur, so it is a kind of beverage.

clue.text: Possibly a type of mail and vice versa

definitions.text: Possibly a type of mail and vice versa

blocks.note: surface reading: a link in armour, the first word in a kind of metal mesh
setter's reading: swap them and the second word is a type of post, so the item is itself mail

explanation.walkthrough: Chain is a type of mail, as in armour, and the reverse holds too: the whole phrase is a kind of post that asks you to forward it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain letter is a message sent by post urging each recipient to send copies on to others.

clue.text: Acquit a criminal performing on water

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A court sets free a lawbreaker who does stunts on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom words acquit and criminal suggest a trial, but acquit and a are just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic sports and displays take place in or upon rivers, lakes or pools.

clue.text: Remark when about to go in cell

indicators.note: about means going around, so the remark wraps around the leaving word

blocks.note: a comment is a remark
to part is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone passes a remark just as they are about to step into a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: About to go reads as one phrase meaning ready to leave; split it into the wrapping signal and the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A compartment is a separate section or division of a larger space, as a cell is.

blocks.note: surface reading: a nasty sketch, or a picture of a wild creature
setter's reading: the pull, or attraction, that a creature exerts

explanation.walkthrough: Drawing suggests a picture; here it means pulling or attracting, and beastly is read literally as belonging to a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an earthy personal allure, and was once Mesmer's term for a supposed force flowing from living bodies.

clue.text: The time when nobody is stopped short

indicators.note: something stopped short does not reach its end, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: nobody is no one

explanation.surface: A moment when no one is halted in their tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: NO ONE loses its last E to leave midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock in the midday, a particular hour on the clock.

blocks.note: to scar is to wound and leave a mark
a tongue is a language
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurts their tongue and also comes down with an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue looks like the body part; it is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina is scarlet fever, and complaint is a common word for an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Member of secret society who got out of bed on the wrong side?

blocks.note: rose, as in got up in the morning
getting out of bed on the wrong side leaves you in a bad mood

explanation.surface: A grumpy member of a hidden fraternity who had a bad start to the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom of getting out of bed on the wrong side means waking up irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rose-Cross is a Rosicrucian, an adherent of the esoteric brotherhood of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Create trouble following naughty child's curse

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters before it are stirred up
following means coming after, so this piece goes at the end

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A badly behaved youngster swears and causes mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: Create trouble reads as a phrase meaning make a fuss; create is the fodder and trouble the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprecate is to call down evil on someone, so as a verb it means to curse.

clue.text: Open wide to take small drink from fount of inspiration

indicators.note: to take in something is to hold it, so the gaping word holds the drink

blocks.note: agape means with the mouth wide open
a nip is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Drinking from the source of creativity with mouth wide open.
explanation.walkthrough: Aganippe is the spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking from Aganippe's waters was said to inspire poets, making it a legendary source of inspiration.

indicators.note: abroad can mean scattered widely, so these letters are spread about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A preacher's representatives make their homes overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist preaches the gospel and travels to spread the faith, which is a missionary's work.

blocks.note: first meaning: a location or site
second meaning: to discern or notice something

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like directions to a lovers' haunt; make out means to discern.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a particular location and a verb for noticing or catching sight of something.

blocks.note: first meaning: played on a wind instrument
second meaning: having grooves cut along it, as a column

explanation.surface: Someone approves of background tunes as being hip.
explanation.walkthrough: Groovy looks like sixties slang for cool; it means literally full of grooves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a tune played on a flute and also a column or glass carved with long channels.

indicators.note: analysis breaks something into its parts, so these letters are taken apart and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An academy that teaches how to get into the study of logic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that analysis is not a subject of study here but a signal to break the letters up.
explanation.definitionFit: A training college is an establishment, typically for teachers, and institute is a general word for such a body.

blocks.note: one hundred per cent is the whole of it
ay is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: Full support for taking a middle course.
explanation.walkthrough: For looks like a link word; it gives a yes vote, spelt AY.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay is to ease or lessen fear or pain, so it means to moderate as a verb.

clue.text: Fine point is taken as relative

indicators.note: something taken is brought in, so the point goes inside the other word

blocks.note: nice means fine, as in a fine distinction
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A subtle argument is accepted as being comparative.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine point reads as one phrase, a subtlety; split, it is a word for fine and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Gather about fifty points when stepping back

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for gather surrounds the number

blocks.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
south and east, two points of the compass

explanation.surface: A sports team racks up fifty points while being pushed backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Points suggests scoring; in crosswords it often means compass points, here S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness or old habits after improvement, a backward step.

blocks.note: workers on strike are out
the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: An actor ostracised by colleagues for joining a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: Striking looks like an adjective meaning impressive; it means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected or excluded by society or a group.

clue.text: Fruit stone from a lot of mountains

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the end of the range's name is dropped

blocks.note: the Pyrenees are the mountains between France and Spain

explanation.surface: A pip or pit found in some mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The range loses its last two letters, ES. PYRENE is a botanical word for the stone of a drupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyrene is the hard seed-bearing kernel inside a fleshy fruit such as a cherry or plum.

blocks.note: a sod is a piece of turf
an animal's den is its lair

explanation.surface: Grass laid on top of an animal's home has been given a good soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through, thoroughly saturated, as ground is after heavy rain.
